Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Singapore River Festival – final days, ends 20 September

2. Mid-Autumn Family FUN – 19–20 September

3. VivoCity's Sanrio Moonlit Garden – continues to 27 September

4. Osteria Mozza opens at ION Orchard – Chef Nancy Silverton

5. Mom's Touch returns to Singapore – Boat Quay

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Beng Hiang brings nearly 48 years of Hokkien heritage to the Garden Terrace, with recipes passed down from the original Chinatown shophouse. Signatures worth flagging to guests include Orh Nee (yam paste dessert) and Hae Bee Hiam (spicy dried shrimp sambal) – dishes that rarely appear on hotel menus outside a genuine Hokkien kitchen.

  • Beng Hiang – Authentic Hokkien Cuisine, Garden Terrace.

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

  • J65 – International Seafood Dinner Buffet. $88++/adult, $44++/child. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

Singapore River Festival wraps up its 10th edition this week, closing on the 20th – worth a final push for any guest who hasn't made it down to the quays yet. The lead-up to Mid-Autumn Festival keeps building too, with VivoCity's Sanrio Moonlit Garden continuing and a dedicated Mid-Autumn Family FUN day landing on the last weekend. On the dining side, this is a genuinely strong week for new openings: Osteria Mozza brings Chef Nancy Silverton's Michelin-starred Cal-Italian cooking to ION Orchard – her only outpost in Asia – while Mom's Touch, one of Korea's largest fried chicken chains, returns to Singapore after a four-year absence.

Mid-Autumn Family FUN

A dedicated family day marking the lead-up to Mid-Autumn Festival, bringing together 25 separate activities in one place – lantern walks, stargazing sessions, hands-on crafts and live performances, designed to give families a full day of celebration without having to piece together separate events across the city.

Event Date: 19–20 September 2026

Best For: Families / Free Activities / Culture Seekers

Concierge Recommendation: A good one-stop option for guests with children who want a genuine Mid-Autumn experience without needing to travel between multiple locations.

VivoCity's Sanrio Moonlit Garden

VivoCity transforms into an illuminated Sanrio wonderland for Mid-Autumn Festival, with six distinct glowing worlds featuring Hello Kitty, My Melody and friends. Beyond the photo-friendly installations, the display includes interactive games and festive activities built around the Mid-Autumn theme.

Event Date: 25 August – 27 September 2026

Location: VivoCity

Admission: Free

Best For: Families / Sanrio Fans / Photography

Concierge Recommendation: Still has over a week left to run – a reliable, free family option for guests staying near HarbourFront or Sentosa.

Restaurants & Bars

Osteria Mozza

Nearly 15 years after first landing in Singapore, Osteria Mozza has reopened on Level 3 of ION Orchard – the only Asian outpost of chef Nancy Silverton's Michelin-starred Cal-Italian concept. Silverton picked up the 2026 James Beard Lifetime Achievement Award this year alone, which says something about the pedigree behind the menu. The Singapore debut here is the Pizza alla Pala, a paddle-shaped Roman-style pizza with a light, airy crumb built for sharing, in flavours like Spicy Tomato and Potato alongside Fennel Sausage and a reworked BLT.

Location: Level 3, ION Orchard

Signature: Pizza alla Pala (from $25); weekday-only Piadina lunch (from $20) – pizza dough folded sando-style with fillings like Chicken Milanese or steak with caramelised onions

Best For: Couples / Italian Cuisine Fans / Something Different

Concierge Recommendation: Worth mentioning specifically that this is chef Nancy Silverton's only restaurant in Asia – a meaningful detail for any guest who knows her work from Los Angeles.

Mom's Touch

One of South Korea's largest fried chicken chains, with over 1,400 outlets there, returns to Singapore after pulling out of the market in 2022. The new outlet sits in a shophouse along Boat Quay – a fitting spot for after-work drinks and fried chicken. The brand has also teamed up with South Korean girl group LE SSERAFIM on three Singapore-exclusive burgers.

Location: 81 South Bridge Road, Boat Quay

Signature: SuperThigh Chicken Burger ($9.95); Boneless Fried Chicken Thigh ($12.95); limited-time Banana Milk Coffee ($4.95)

Best For: Casual Dining / Korean Food Fans / Late-Night Bites

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, casual pick for guests wanting something different from the usual Boat Quay dinner options – easy to combine with drinks along the river.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Lawry's The Prime Rib

An internationally renowned name in prime rib dining, with a legacy stretching back more than 80 years and franchise locations across Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Middle East. The Singapore outlet keeps the tradition intact: the Signature Prime Rib is aged 28 days, slow-roasted on a bed of rock salt, and carved tableside from the restaurant's iconic Silver Cart – as much a piece of theatre as it is a meal.

Current Promotion: Check for the latest seasonal set menu.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required for standard bookings; deposit of $50 per person required for groups of 8 or more.

Hours: Sun–Thu 11:30am–10:00pm; Fri, Sat & Eve of PH 11:30am–10:30pm

Contact: +65 6836 3333 / reservations@lawrys.com.sg

Address: 333A Orchard Road, #04-01/31, Mandarin Gallery, Singapore 238897

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable, theatrical choice for guests wanting a classic steakhouse experience – the tableside carving from the Silver Cart is worth mentioning in advance, since it's part of what makes the meal memorable.

True Blue Cuisine

Opened in 2003 in the heart of Katong before moving to Armenian Street in 2008, right beside the Peranakan Museum, True Blue Cuisine has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand for years running. Owner-chef Benjamin Seck built the restaurant around preserving Peranakan culture as much as the food itself – the dining room is filled with antique Peranakan furniture and tableware, giving the space a museum-like quality without feeling stiff or overly formal.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for festive set menus.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required to book.

Hours: Mon–Sat, 11:30am–2:30pm & 5:30pm–9:30pm. Closed Sunday and public holidays.

Contact: +65 6440 0449

Address: 47/49 Armenian Street, Singapore 179937

Signature: Ayam Buah Keluak – chicken thighs stewed in a rich black nut gravy

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for guests who want the cultural storytelling alongside the meal, not just the food – easy to pair with a Peranakan Museum visit next door. Remind guests it's closed Sundays.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel or leadership announcements to report this week – all previously featured properties remain unchanged. Colleagues should continue monitoring for updates ahead of NoMad Singapore's late-2026 opening.

Transport & Operational Updates

Singapore River Festival – Final Days

The festival wraps up on 20 September – expect continued heavier foot traffic around Boat Quay, Clarke Quay and Robertson Quay through the final weekend.

Woodsville Tunnel Overnight Closures

The Woodsville Tunnel will see several overnight closures this week to facilitate maintenance works, from 12:01am to 5:00am: Serangoon Road to Woodsville Tunnel (northbound) on 16 September; Upper Serangoon Road to Woodsville Tunnel (southbound) on 15 and 17 September; and MacPherson Road to Woodsville Tunnel on 18 September. Alternative routes via Upper Serangoon Road or Bendemeer Road are signposted on site.

TPE/PIE Slip Road Works Continue

The ongoing overnight bridge works affecting slip roads between Tampines Ave 7, Loyang Ave and the TPE/PIE continue this week, from 14 to 18 September, 10:00pm to 5:30am. This is part of a recurring series that has been running since early September.

Grab Travel Pass – Precinct Discounts

STB and Grab have launched enhanced Travel Pass ride vouchers to encourage exploration of Singapore's neighbourhoods, including after-dark discounts to key precincts. Worth mentioning to guests planning an evening out beyond the usual tourist areas – ask at the desk for current voucher details.

Looking Ahead

Singapore Tennis Open – WTA 500

The newly upgraded Singapore Tennis Open runs 21–27 September at OCBC Arena, among the top-tier events on the WTA calendar – tickets from $8.

Grand Prix Season Singapore 2026

The city-wide build-up to the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix begins in earnest from 2 October, with race-themed lifestyle experiences planned across multiple precincts ahead of the race itself on 9–11 October.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Singapore River Festival closes 20 September – this is the final weekend, not a routine mention.

  • Osteria Mozza is chef Nancy Silverton's only restaurant in Asia – a good detail to lead with for guests familiar with her Los Angeles restaurants.

  • True Blue Cuisine is closed on Sundays and public holidays – confirm before recommending.

  • Grab's enhanced Travel Pass vouchers are worth mentioning proactively to guests planning evening outings – ask at the desk for current details.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Last Call for the River Festival

Evening: Singapore River Festival – pick a quay (Boat Quay, Clarke Quay or Robertson Quay) for the final weekend before it wraps up on the 20th.

Tip: Dinner at Mom's Touch on Boat Quay beforehand is an easy, casual pairing with the festival atmosphere along the river.

Full Day — Orchard Road & Mid-Autumn

Afternoon: Lunch at Osteria Mozza, ION Orchard, then browse Orchard Road.

Evening: VivoCity's Sanrio Moonlit Garden, or Mid-Autumn Family FUN if travelling with children and the dates align (19–20 September).

Tip: ION Orchard and VivoCity are both easily reached by MRT with no transfers needed – a low-effort day for guests without a car.

2 Days — Heritage & Riverside

Day 1

Morning: Peranakan Museum, then lunch at True Blue Cuisine next door. Afternoon: Armenian Street and the Civic District. Evening: Singapore River Festival.

Day 2

Afternoon: Orchard Road shopping, lunch at Osteria Mozza. Evening: Dinner at Lawry's The Prime Rib for the tableside carving experience.

Tip: True Blue Cuisine and the Peranakan Museum are a natural pairing – suggest booking lunch right after the museum visit rather than separately.

Quick Reference

Best Last-Chance Pick: Singapore River Festival (closes 20 September)

Best Free Family Day: Mid-Autumn Family FUN

Best Free Photo Op: VivoCity's Sanrio Moonlit Garden

Best New Restaurant: Osteria Mozza

Best Casual Comeback: Mom's Touch

Best Classic Steakhouse: Lawry's The Prime Rib

Best Cultural Dining: True Blue Cuisine
